scope: Proposition 5.1 (Transverse products) of the manuscript “Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields” (preprints/Arithmeticity-of-twisted-finite-correspondences-for-lattices-over-local-fields-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 286 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1d070a5c4cd8496), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix face types, a thickness bound, and sufficiently small compact transverse face patches at the basepoint o. Suppose the supports of f and g lie within that thickness of the respective positive cones, with all specified positive gaps sufficiently large, and that the ideal directions of po and q−1o belong to the fixed transverse patches. Then µ(qp) = µ(q) + µ(p) + O(1), where the error is uniform on the supports. The product in (5.1) has a uniform tracial L2 bound in either of the following situations: (i) For each coordinate contributed by both cones, one of its two supports is restricted to a moving interval of a fixed bounded width. The separate cutoff factors may be arbitrary uniformly bounded functions. (ii) One of the face types is a single vertex. The cutoff factors are smooth with uniformly bounded sufficiently high seminorms in fixed compact normalized matrix charts; at finite places this means locally constant with a uniformly bounded level. To specify the retained cutoffs in the estimate, write f = hAf1 and g = hBg1. In case (i), these four factors may be arbitrary uniformly bounded scalar functions. In case (ii), each factor has the smooth seminorm bounds or fixed clopen level just specified. Then (5.2) (DgB0)(Df A0) 2 2 ≤ C∥A0∥∞∥B0∥∞∥DhA A0∥2∥DhB B0∥2. The constant includes the stated bounds on the scalar factors. The same estimate holds for a joint symbol, meaning the bilinear Fourier sum X q,p hB(q)hA(p)m(q, p)bqap wqwp, where wqwp is the actual twisted monomial product and m is a smooth joint function on the fixed compact normalized charts, with sufficiently many uniformly bounded derivatives. At finite places use a fixed clopen level. The support and transverse restrictions remain in force. Consequently an additional smooth cutoff factor whose one-column Hilbert norm tends to zero makes the product tend to zero, provided the other bounds and the other cut Hilbert norm remain bounded. In particular, for a fixed finite trace of mass t, (DgB0)(Df A0) 2 ≤ C √ t ∥A0∥∞∥B0∥∞.
